Senses.Explanation: Literally, "go along with it." In the named Dasui case, a monk asks whether "this" is destroyed when the world is destroyed by the kalpa fire. Dasui answers, "destroyed." The monk asks, "then it goes along with it?" and Dasui answers, "go along with it." Later collections repeatedly set this answer beside Longji's contrary "not destroyed" and preserve it as the case's answer-line. Elsewhere the same ordinary phrase can mean following a person or thing; the fixed Chan deployment is its repeated use for Dasui's answer.
Senses.Note: 209 occurrences in 87 allowlisted texts. The master's name has two written forms, "Dasui" (大隋) and the homophonous "Dasui" (大隨); the answer varies between "go along with it" (隨他去) and "go along with it, go along with it" (隨他隨他去). These are transmission variants, not separate senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧遂問刼火洞然大千俱壞未審此箇性壞不壞師云壞進云恁麼則隨他去也師云隨他隨他去也
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 古尊宿語錄, record of Dasui's world-ending-fire exchange. Dasui Fazhen is the exact answering speaker of the repeated stored phrase: an unnamed monk first advances, 'then it goes along with it,' and Dasui replies, 'go along with it, go along with it.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問大隋。劫火洞然大千俱壞。未審這箇壞不壞隋云。壞僧云。恁麼則隨他去也隋云。隨他去。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record of Chan Master Foguo Yuanwu (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄), case twenty-nine. After an unnamed monk asks whether it follows the ruined cosmos, Dasui Fazhen is the exact respondent who repeats, 'it follows it' (隨他去).
